title: ldct-io: read, reconstruct and measure real CT projection data (DICOM-CT-PD)
description:
A Python package (MIT) for working with real CT projection data as distributed by The Cancer Imaging Archive in DICOM-CT-PD form. It restores acquisition order from headers rather than from filenames, which in that format are assigned in an order unrelated to the scan; rebins helical fan-beam projections to single slices; reconstructs by filtered backprojection with selectable apodisation; and measures the physical quantities task-based image quality is built on, including a slanted-edge modulation transfer function taken from a phantom's own outer edge.

It exists so that a measurement made on a physical scanner can be re-derived from the archived projections rather than taken on trust. The reconstruction is checked against closed-form answers in the test suite rather than against a stored output of itself.

No imaging data is redistributed. The projections are identified by Series Instance UID and obtained from The Cancer Imaging Archive under their own licence; what travels in this repository is the code, the manifest and the derived numbers.

Version 0.2.0 adds the measurement the package was built to support. It inserts a lesion of known size and contrast into real anatomy and scores detection with a cross-fitted prewhitening observer on paired trials, so that the background cancels and the noise does not; it trains a residual denoiser against a least-squares adversarial critic as well as against fidelity, changing the objective and nothing else, to supply an arm capable of fabricating structure; it reduces dose in the photon counts, where the square-root law is a consequence of a Poisson draw rather than an assumption; and it reports how far a held-out ranking depends on which regions of interest were admitted.
